reasons: The file contains direct expected-value tests for each formatter.
I did not run these tests in this review.

terms.meaning: the test runner this project uses for frontend tests
fixed test data used so a test gives the same result each time

sections.name: File setup
sections.title: Test imports and fixture
sections.what: Loads the generated artifacts file and the functions under test.
sections.why: So the evidence tests run against real data, not invented data.
sections.watch_out: The test fails to load if the generated file is missing.

sections.name: money
sections.title: Money formatting tests
sections.what: Checks that small amounts keep their decimals, zero shows as zero, larger amounts round to whole units, the minus sign sits on the amount, and no bare number is printed.
sections.why: The comments say an earlier rounding rule once showed a real sub-unit cost as a whole unit and made a small cost look free.
sections.watch_out: These expectations encode the rounding rule on purpose. Changing the rule will break them.

sections.name: units
sections.title: Unit formatting tests
sections.what: Checks that shares of effort, FTE, bands and percentages each show their unit.
sections.why: Units stop a reader from having to guess what a number measures.
sections.watch_out: The band test expects one exact layout, so changing its spacing or order breaks it.

sections.name: the evidence index (part 1)
sections.title: Evidence lookup tests, first half
sections.what: Checks that every pack is indexed, that a real id resolves, that a fake id is reported as dangling, and that a mixed list is split correctly.
sections.why: A comment says the dangling path never ran on the real data, so a direct test was added to exercise it.
sections.watch_out: The test takes the first id from the data, so it needs at least one item to exist.

sections.name: the evidence index: for
sections.title: Evidence lookup tests, second half
sections.what: Checks that each authority tier from 1 to 4 has a label, that an unknown tier says unmapped, and that every id cited by every record resolves against a pack.
sections.why: Makes sure no real record cites an id that does not exist.
sections.watch_out: The walk looks for keys whose names end in evidence id, so renaming those keys could make it find nothing without failing. The test guards against this by requiring at least one cited id.

summary: Tests that the number and text formatters show the right unit, rounding and sign, and that evidence lookups work on real data.
purpose: Catches a formatter change that would hide a real cost, drop a unit or mislabel a source.
why: The comments explain that whole-unit rounding once hid a real sub-unit cost, so these cases were written to guard it.
how: Loads the generated artifacts file, then runs each formatter against fixed inputs and expected outputs. Also builds the evidence index from the real data and tests resolution on real and fake ids.
inputs: The generated artifacts file and fixed test values.
outputs: Pass or fail results for each test in the vitest runner.
risks: Some tests depend on the golden data having at least one item and at least four cases. If that data changes, these tests can fail for reasons unrelated to the formatters.
debug: If a money test fails, check the rounding threshold in format.ts. If an evidence test fails, check that the artifacts file was rebuilt.
